summary: A guard keeps vigil over a city and a leopard watches its prey. Jeremiah applies the verb to Yahweh’s resolve to carry out his word, whether to uproot or to plant.

stems.gloss: stay awake, keep watch, watch over, give sustained attention

senses.definition: Remain awake or attend closely to a place, person or thing.

evidence.note: The psalmist lies awake like a lone bird on a rooftop.
The city watchman stays awake through his watch.
A leopard watches the cities for anyone coming out.
The listener waits at Wisdom’s doors every day.
Those entrusted with the offerings must keep watch until they weigh them out.

senses.definition: Attend to a purpose so as to bring it about.

evidence.note: Yahweh is watching over his word to perform it, echoing the almond branch in the preceding verse.
The same vigilance attends the acts of uprooting and planting.
Yahweh watches over the Judeans in Egypt to bring the announced harm.
Daniel recalls that Yahweh watched over the threatened disaster and brought it about.
People intent on wrongdoing are among those to be cut off.

note: Job.21.32 also uses the verb at a burial mound. The identity of the one keeping watch there is uncertain.
